what_its_for: Cholic acid is used to treat certain rare liver problems that you are born with. These include bile acid synthesis disorders (problems with how your liver makes bile acids) and problems caused by a condition called Zellweger spectrum disorder. It helps your liver work better by replacing the bile acids your body cannot make properly, which helps with digestion and protects your liver from damage.
how_to_take: Take cholic acid capsules by mouth, with food. Swallow the capsule whole with a full glass of water. If you or your child cannot swallow the capsule whole, you may open it and mix the powder into a small amount of infant formula, expressed breast milk, or soft food like mashed potatoes. Take it right away after mixing and do not save it for later. Always take it with a meal or snack.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose based on your body weight. The usual dose is about 10 to 15 mg per kilogram of body weight per day, taken as a single dose once daily or split into two doses. Never change your dose without talking to your doctor first. Your doctor will check blood and urine tests regularly to make sure the dose is right for you.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still the same day. If it is the next day already, skip the missed dose and just take your next regular dose at the usual time. Do not take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store cholic acid capsules at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed. Store it in a dry place away from moisture and heat. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it after the expiration date printed on the bottle.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking cholic acid at the same time as medicines that can interfere with it. Specifically, tell your doctor if you take bile acid binders like cholestyramine, colestipol, or colesevelam, or antacids containing aluminum hydroxide, as these can block cholic acid from being absorbed into your body. If you must take these medicines, take them at a different time of day — ask your pharmacist how to space them out. Avoid stopping this medicine on your own without talking to your doctor, as your condition may get worse.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you notice: yellowing of your skin or the whites of your eyes (jaundice), dark brown or tea-colored urine, very pale or clay-colored stools, severe stomach pain or swelling, unusual tiredness or weakness, nausea or vomiting that does not go away, or signs of liver problems getting worse. These may be signs that your dose needs to be adjusted or that there is a problem with your liver. Go to the emergency room immediately if you feel very ill.
when_it_works: Cholic acid does not cure your condition, but it helps manage it over time. You may not feel a dramatic change right away. Improvement in liver tests and symptoms may be noticed over several weeks to months of regular use. It is important to keep taking it every day as prescribed, even if you feel well, because stopping it can cause your condition to get worse quickly.
special_populations: Children: Cholic acid is approved for use in children, including newborns, and is one of the few medicines approved for these rare conditions in pediatric patients. Doses are based on weight and will be carefully adjusted by your doctor. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, talk to your doctor before using this medicine. The safety during pregnancy and breastfeeding is not fully known. Elderly patients: There is limited information about use in elderly patients, but dose adjustments may be needed based on overall health and liver function. Always tell your doctor about all your medical conditions and all medicines you are taking.
